questions.text: What is one work decision you keep telling yourself you'll make 'later,' and what does 'later' actually protect you from right now?
If you knew the next thing you tried at work would fail, but no one would ever find out, what would you attempt?
Whose career are you quietly measuring yours against, and what do you think their life actually costs them that you can't see?
When you imagine yourself five years into this line of work, what part of that picture makes you uneasy?
What piece of work are you holding back because it isn't 'ready,' and who is waiting on it while you keep polishing?
What at work would you have to trust someone else with in order to grow, and what are you afraid they'd do differently?
You've called this job either your dream or a dead end. What's the more honest, in-between version of it?
Think of a recent 'yes' you gave someone. If you're honest, what were you really afraid would happen if you'd said no?
Which conversation have you been putting off, and what do you imagine the silence is costing the other person?
Where in a relationship are you managing someone else's feelings that aren't actually yours to manage?
When was the last time someone truly saw you, and what did they notice that you rarely let people see?
After a hard conversation, what's the story you tell yourself about your part in it, and how much of that story is actually fair?
You've decided this person is either with you or against you. What evidence are you leaving out to keep it that clean?
What conversation do you keep replaying, and what are you hoping to find in it the hundredth time that wasn't there the first?
What's the small daily thing you keep avoiding, and what feeling shows up in the moment right before you turn away from it?
Which habit have you abandoned because you couldn't do it 'properly,' and what would 'good enough' have looked like instead?
When you miss one day of something you're building, what do you tell yourself the whole streak now means?
Which of your routines are you keeping out of genuine choice, and which are just momentum you never stopped to question?
When you slip on a habit, whose voice is it that criticizes you, and would you ever speak that way to someone you love?
What are you trying to hold together through your routines, and what happens inside you when one of them breaks?
You've committed to changing several things at once. Which one actually matters most, and which are you adding to avoid facing that one?
Look at everything you've said yes to this month. Which of these did you take on to feel needed rather than because it was yours to carry?
Whose approval are you running on empty to keep, and what would it cost you to disappoint them just once?
What standard are you holding yourself to right now that no one else asked for, and who taught you it wasn't safe to lower it?
When did you last rest without earning it first, and what makes rest feel like something you have to deserve?
What would you have to let go badly for a while in order to stop running yourself into the ground?
At night, what unfinished thing keeps looping in your head, and what would it take to set it down until morning?
If you had to cut one commitment tomorrow, which would you protect the hardest, and what does that tell you about where your worth is tied up?
What goal have you stopped talking about because it started to feel real, and what does that quiet tell you?
What would you begin this week if you fully accepted that you might be bad at it at first?
Whose progress makes you feel behind, and what race did you agree to run that no one actually entered you in?
Think back to the last time you felt genuinely driven. What was present then that's missing now?
What plan are you endlessly refining instead of starting, and what would a rough first attempt actually risk?
When your motivation dips, what do you conclude about yourself, and is that a fact or just a well-worn habit of thought?
You've decided you're either 'on' or 'off,' disciplined or lazy. What does the messy middle of a real week actually look like for you?
What's the harshest thing you've called yourself this week, and would you accept anyone else describing you that way?
Whose highlight reel are you comparing your behind-the-scenes to, and what would shift if you stopped?
How much of what you did today was for you, and how much was to be seen as good by someone else?
If your worth had nothing to do with what you produce, what would you do differently tomorrow?
What would you stop apologizing for if you believed failing at it wouldn't make you any less worthy?
What old moment do you keep returning to as proof of something bad about you, and who decided it meant that?
At work, when you feel 'not enough,' whose standard are you failing — theirs, or one you inherited and never chose?
What's the first tiny step of the thing you keep meaning to start, and what makes even that step feel too big to take?
Whose expectations shaped the path you're on, and what would you choose if their opinion genuinely didn't factor in?
Who in your life gets your best energy, and who gets whatever's left, and how did you decide that order?
When you 'fall off,' do you rebuild slowly or wait to start over 'properly on Monday' — and where does that leave the days in between?
When someone gives you a compliment, what do you actually do with it, and what would it mean to just let it land?
What are you proving by staying the busiest person in the room, and who exactly are you proving it to?
Where are you keeping the peace at the cost of telling the truth, and what does that peace actually preserve?
What ambition have you quietly shrunk to a 'realistic' size so it couldn't hurt you if it didn't work out?
Which of your daily habits genuinely restore you, and which just help you numb until tomorrow?
What would you attempt if you trusted that your value wouldn't rise or fall with the result?
If money were handled for the next year, what work would you still want to do, and what does that answer point to?
Where do you try to run other people's routines or choices, and what fear sits underneath needing them to do it your way?
When you finally have a free hour, where does your mind go — to rest, or straight back to the thing you couldn't resolve?
What would you have to believe about yourself to let a piece of work be 'done' rather than perfect?
Who have you been slowly pulling away from, and what would you have to feel if you moved back toward them?
When you see how someone else seems to live, what do you assume about their discipline, and what might that assumption be costing you?
What part of your work makes you lose track of time, and how much of your actual week contains any of it?
If your body could speak plainly right now, what do you think it's been trying to tell you that you keep overriding?
